questions.explanation: Traditional inter-VLAN routing uses one physical router port per VLAN. Router-on-a-stick uses subinterfaces to connect multiple logical networks to a single physical router port.

questions.question: Subinterface G0/1.10 on R1 must be configured as the default gateway for the VLAN 10 192.168.10.0/24 network. Which command should be configured on the subinterface to enable inter-VLAN routing for VLAN 10?
questions.explanation: The subinterface must be assigned to VLAN 10 using the encapsulation dot1q 10 command. The switchport commands are switch configuration commands, and encapsulation vlan 10 is not valid.

questions.question: What is important to consider while configuring the subinterfaces of a router when implementing inter-VLAN routing?
options: The IP address of each subinterface must be the default gateway address for each VLAN subnet.
The no shutdown command must be given on each subinterface.
The physical interface must have an IP address configured.
The subinterface numbers must match the VLAN ID number.
questions.explanation: Hosts in each VLAN need a default gateway. The router subinterface IP address should be configured as the default gateway address for that VLAN subnet.

questions.question: What are the steps that must be completed in order to enable inter-VLAN routing using router-on-a-stick?
options: Configure the physical interfaces on the router and enable a routing protocol.
Create the VLANs on the router and define the port membership assignments on the switch.
Create the VLANs on the switch to include port membership assignment and enable a routing protocol on the router.
Create the VLANs on the switch to include port membership assignment and configure subinterfaces on the router matching the VLANs.
questions.explanation: For router-on-a-stick, create the VLANs and port memberships on the switch, configure the switch port to the router as a trunk, and configure router subinterfaces that match the VLANs.

questions.question: What two statements are true regarding the use of subinterfaces for inter-VLAN routing?
options: Fewer router Ethernet ports required than in traditional inter-VLAN routing
Less complex physical connection than in traditional inter-VLAN routing
More switch ports required than in traditional inter-VLAN routing
Simpler Layer 3 troubleshooting than with traditional inter-VLAN routing
Subinterfaces have no contention for bandwidth
questions.explanation: Traditional inter-VLAN routing requires more physical ports and connections. Router-on-a-stick with subinterfaces requires fewer router Ethernet ports and has a less complex physical connection.

questions.question: Which router-on-a-stick command and prompt on R1 correctly encapsulates 802.1Q traffic for VLAN 20?
questions.explanation: The encapsulation dot1q vlan_id [native] command is configured in subinterface configuration mode. Therefore the correct prompt and command are R1(config-subif)# encapsulation dot1q 20.

questions.question: What are two disadvantages of using the router-on-a-stick inter-VLAN routing method in a large network?
options: It requires multiple physical interfaces on a router.
It requires subinterfaces to be configured on the same subnets.
questions.explanation: Router-on-a-stick requires a router to route traffic between VLANs and does not scale easily in large networks. Multiple subinterfaces can also affect traffic flow speed, so large networks typically use Layer 3 switches.

questions.question: What is a characteristic of a routed port on a Layer 3 switch?
options: It requires the switchport mode access interface config command.
It requires the no switchport interface config command.
It requires the switchport access vlan vlan-id interface config command.
questions.explanation: A routed port is created on a Layer 3 switch by disabling Layer 2 switchport behavior with the no switchport command. Routed ports can then be configured with an IPv4 address and do not support Layer 2 trunking or access VLAN assignment.

questions.question: What are two advantages of using a Layer 3 switch with SVIs for inter-VLAN routing?
options: It switches packets faster than using the router-on-a-stick method.
SVIs can be bundled into EtherChannels.
SVIs can be divided using subinterfaces.
SVIs eliminate the need for a default gateway in the hosts.
questions.explanation: Layer 3 switches provide inter-VLAN routing without requiring a separate router and use hardware-based switching for higher packet processing rates than router-on-a-stick.

questions.question: An EtherChannel link using LACP was formed between two switches, S1 and S2. While verifying the configuration, which mode combination could be utilized on both switches?
questions.explanation: An EtherChannel link using LACP forms when both sides are active, or when one side is active and the other is passive. Passive/passive will not initiate negotiation, and on mode does not use LACP.

questions.question: When a range of ports is being configured for EtherChannel, which mode will configure PAgP so that it initiates the EtherChannel negotiation?
questions.explanation: The channel-group mode desirable command enables PAgP unconditionally and initiates negotiation. Auto waits to receive PAgP packets. Active and passive are LACP modes.

questions.question: Which three interface parameters must match for an EtherChannel to form?
questions.explanation: For EtherChannel, trunking mode, native VLAN, and allowed VLANs must match. Some negotiation modes can be different and still form a channel, such as active/passive or desirable/auto.

questions.question: What are three advantages of using EtherChannel technology?
options: Configuration tasks can be done on the EtherChannel interface.
A spanning tree recalculation is not required when a single link within the channel goes down.
The Spanning Tree Protocol shuts down the unused interfaces in the bundle to avoid loops.
There is no need to upgrade links to faster connections to increase bandwidth.
EtherChannel uses multiple logical links to provide redundancy.
Load balancing is not needed with EtherChannel.
questions.explanation: Configuration can be applied to the EtherChannel interface, existing ports can be bundled to increase bandwidth, and STP does not recalculate if only one member link fails. EtherChannel is one logical link and supports load balancing.

questions.question: A network administrator is configuring an EtherChannel link between two physical ports on a switch. Which statement describes the result when one of the physical ports fails?
options: The EtherChannel stops transmitting data until it is restarted.
The EtherChannel continues transmitting data with reduced bandwidth.
questions.explanation: EtherChannel is seen as one logical connection. If one member link fails, the channel remains functional but has reduced bandwidth, and STP recalculation is not required.

questions.question: When EtherChannel is implemented, multiple physical interfaces are bundled into which type of logical connection?
questions.explanation: EtherChannel bundles physical interfaces into a logical port-channel interface.

questions.question: When a range of ports is being configured for EtherChannel by the use of PAgP, which mode will form the bundled channel only if the port receives PAgP packets from another device?
questions.explanation: The channel-group mode auto command enables PAgP only if the port receives a PAgP packet. Desirable actively initiates PAgP. Active and passive are LACP modes.

questions.question: Which two load balancing methods can be implemented with EtherChannel technology?
questions.explanation: Source MAC to destination MAC and source IP to destination IP are two load balancing methods used with EtherChannel.

questions.question: Which function is provided by EtherChannel?
options: enabling traffic from multiple VLANs to travel over a single Layer 2 link
spreading traffic across multiple physical WAN links
dividing the bandwidth of a single link into separate time slots
creating one logical link by using multiple physical links between two LAN switches
questions.explanation: EtherChannel groups several Fast Ethernet or Gigabit switch ports into one logical channel.

questions.question: Which statement is true about EtherChannel technology?
options: All configuration tasks must be done on the individual ports in the EtherChannel link.
STP does not run on redundant EtherChannel links.
Links must be upgraded to support EtherChannel.
questions.explanation: EtherChannel uses existing switch ports, so links do not have to be upgraded. STP still operates on EtherChannel, and configuration may be done on member ports or on the port-channel interface depending on the task.

questions.question: Which two mode combinations would result in the successful negotiation of an EtherChannel?
questions.explanation: Valid EtherChannel combinations include on/on, active/passive, active/active, desirable/auto, and desirable/desirable.

questions.question: Which two protocols are link aggregation protocols?
questions.explanation: PAgP and LACP, also known as IEEE 802.3ad, can be used to form EtherChannel. STP and RSTP prevent Layer 2 loops.

questions.question: When a range of ports is being configured for EtherChannel, which mode will configure LACP so that it initiates the EtherChannel negotiation?
questions.explanation: The channel-group mode active command enables LACP unconditionally and initiates negotiation. Passive waits for LACP packets. Desirable and auto are PAgP modes.

questions.question: What will happen if a network administrator puts a port that is part of an EtherChannel bundle into a different VLAN than the other ports in that bundle?
options: The EtherChannel bundle will stay up if the ports were configured with no negotiation between the switches to form the EtherChannel.
The EtherChannel bundle will stay up if either PAgP or LACP is used.
The EtherChannel bundle will stay up only if LACP is used.
The EtherChannel bundle will stay up only if PAgP is used.
questions.explanation: All ports in an EtherChannel bundle must either be trunk ports or be access ports in the same VLAN. If VLAN settings do not match, the EtherChannel fails.

questions.question: When a range of ports is being configured for EtherChannel, which mode will configure LACP on a port only if the port receives LACP packets from another device?
questions.explanation: The channel-group mode passive command enables LACP only if the port receives an LACP packet from another device.

questions.question: There has been an increase in network traffic between two Catalyst 2960 switches, and their FastEthernet trunk link has reached its capacity. How can traffic flow be improved?
options: Add routers between the switches to create additional broadcast domains.
Configure smaller VLANs to decrease the size of the collision domain.
Increase the speed of the ports using the bandwidth command.
questions.explanation: Bundling physical ports with EtherChannel increases available bandwidth between switches. Adding VLANs or routers does not solve trunk congestion, and the bandwidth command does not increase physical port speed.

questions.question: Which statement is true regarding the use of PAgP to create EtherChannels?
options: It increases the number of ports that are participating in spanning tree.
It mandates that an even number of ports (2, 4, 6, etc.) be used for aggregation.
It requires more physical links than LACP does
questions.explanation: PAgP is Cisco proprietary and automatically aggregates ports into an EtherChannel between Cisco devices. LACP can be used with Cisco and non-Cisco devices.

questions.question: Which combination of channel-group modes will establish an EtherChannel?
options: Switch 1 set to auto; switch 2 set to auto.
Switch 1 set to auto; switch 2 set to on.
Switch 1 set to desirable; switch 2 set to desirable.
Switch 1 set to on; switch 2 set to desirable.
questions.explanation: Desirable/desirable forms an EtherChannel because both sides actively negotiate. On mode does not negotiate, and auto/auto does not initiate negotiation.

questions.question: Which interface configuration command will enable the port to initiate an LACP EtherChannel?
questions.explanation: The channel-group mode active command enables LACP unconditionally and initiates negotiation. Passive waits for LACP packets.

questions.question: Which interface configuration command will enable the port to establish an EtherChannel only if it receives PAgP packets from the other switch?
questions.explanation: The channel-group mode auto command enables PAgP only if the port receives a PAgP packet from another device.

questions.question: Which statement describes a characteristic of EtherChannel?
options: It can combine up to a maximum of 4 physical links.
It can bundle mixed types of 100 Mbps and 1 Gbps Ethernet links.
It consists of multiple parallel links between a switch and a router.
It is made by combining multiple physical links that are seen as one link between two switches.
questions.explanation: EtherChannel combines multiple compatible Ethernet physical links so they are seen and configured as one logical link. Each EtherChannel can commonly include up to eight compatible Ethernet ports.

questions.question: What are two advantages of using LACP?
options: LACP allows automatic formation of EtherChannel links.
LACP allows use of multivendor devices.
LACP decreases the amount of configuration that is needed on a switch for EtherChannel.
LACP eliminates the need for the Spanning Tree Protocol.
LACP increases redundancy to Layer 3 devices.
LACP provides a simulated environment for testing link aggregation.
questions.explanation: LACP is part of IEEE 802.3ad and allows automatic EtherChannel negotiation by sending LACP packets. Because it is standards-based, it can be used in multivendor environments.

questions.question: Which three settings must match in order for switch ports to form an EtherChannel?
options: Non-trunk ports must belong to the same VLAN.
Port security violation settings on interconnecting ports must match.
The duplex settings on interconnecting ports must match.
The port channel group number on interconnecting switches must match.
The SNMP community strings must match.
The speed settings on interconnecting ports must match.
questions.explanation: All interfaces in an EtherChannel must have matching speed and duplex settings. If they are not trunks, they must belong to the same VLAN. SNMP strings and port security settings are not relevant to EtherChannel formation.

questions.question: Which statement is true about broadcast and collision domains?
options: The size of the collision domain can be reduced by adding hubs to a network.
Adding a switch to a network will increase the size of the broadcast domain.
Adding a router to a network will increase the size of the collision domain.
The more interfaces a router has the larger the resulting broadcast domain.
questions.explanation: A switch forwards broadcast frames out all other interfaces, including interfaces connected to other switches. Adding more switches can increase the size of the broadcast domain.

questions.question: What is one function of a Layer 2 switch?
options: forwards data based on logical addressing
determines which interface is used to forward a frame based on the destination MAC address
duplicates the electrical signal of each frame to every port
learns the port assigned to a host by examining the destination MAC address
questions.explanation: A Layer 2 switch uses the destination MAC address to look up the associated port in the MAC address table and forwards the frame to that port. It learns MAC addresses by examining source MAC addresses in inbound frames.

questions.question: What is the significant difference between a hub and a Layer 2 LAN switch?
options: A hub divides collision domains, and a switch divides broadcast domains.
Each port of a hub is a collision domain, and each port of a switch is a broadcast domain.
A switch creates many smaller collision domains, and a hub increases the size of a single collision domain.
A hub forwards frames, and a switch forwards only packets.
questions.explanation: Hubs operate at the physical layer and extend a single collision domain. Switches forward frames at Layer 2, and each switch port is a separate collision domain.

questions.question: What will a Cisco LAN switch do if it receives an incoming frame and the destination MAC address is not listed in the MAC address table?
options: Send the frame to the default gateway address.
Use ARP to resolve the port that is related to the frame.
Forward the frame out all ports except the port where the frame is received.
questions.explanation: When the destination MAC address is unknown, a switch floods the frame out all ports except the ingress port. When the destination device replies, the switch learns its source MAC address and port.

questions.question: Which switch characteristic helps alleviate network congestion when a 10 Gbps port is forwarding data to a 1 Gbps port?
questions.explanation: Frame buffers store ingress traffic until the slower egress port can transmit it. This helps reduce dropped frames and alleviate congestion.

questions.question: Which switching method makes use of the FCS value?
questions.explanation: Store-and-forward switching receives the entire frame and checks the frame-check sequence (FCS) before forwarding.

questions.question: What does the term “port density” represent for an Ethernet switch?
options: the memory space that is allocated to each switch port
the numbers of hosts that are connected to each switch port
questions.explanation: Port density is the number of ports available on a switch.

questions.question: Which information does a switch use to keep the MAC address table information current?
options: the source MAC address and the incoming port
the source and destination MAC addresses and the incoming port
the source and destination MAC addresses and the outgoing port
the destination MAC address and the incoming port
the source MAC address and the outgoing port
the destination MAC address and the outgoing port
questions.explanation: A switch maintains its MAC address table by using the source MAC address of incoming frames and the port on which those frames arrive.

questions.question: Which two statements are true about half-duplex and full-duplex communications?
options: Half duplex has only one channel.
Full duplex increases the effective bandwidth.
Full duplex allows both ends to transmit and receive simultaneously.
Full duplex offers 100 percent potential use of the bandwidth.
All modern NICS support both half-duplex and full-duplex communication.
questions.explanation: Full-duplex communication allows both ends to transmit and receive simultaneously, increasing effective bandwidth. Gigabit Ethernet and 10 Gb/s NICs require full duplex and do not support half-duplex operation.

questions.question: Which type of address does a switch use to build the MAC address table?
questions.explanation: A switch builds the MAC address table from the source MAC address in received frames and associates that address with the ingress port.

questions.question: Which option correctly describes a switching method?
options: cut-through: makes a forwarding decision after receiving the entire frame
cut-through: provides the flexibility to support any mix of Ethernet speeds
store-and-forward: forwards the frame immediately after examining its destination MAC address
store-and-forward: ensures that the frame is free of physical and data-link errors
questions.explanation: Store-and-forward switching receives the entire frame and performs error checking before forwarding. Cut-through switching begins forwarding after reading the destination MAC address.

questions.question: Which network device can serve as a boundary to divide a Layer 2 broadcast domain?
questions.explanation: Only a Layer 3 device, such as a router, can divide a Layer 2 broadcast domain.

questions.question: What is the purpose of frame buffers on a switch?
options: They execute checksum values before transmission.
They provide temporary storage of the frame checksum.
They hold traffic, thus alleviating network congestion.
They provide a basic security scan on received frames.
questions.explanation: Frame buffers store traffic waiting to be transmitted, which helps prevent drops when traffic arrives faster than it can leave.

questions.question: Which network device can be used to eliminate collisions on an Ethernet network?
questions.explanation: A switch provides microsegmentation. Each switch port is its own collision domain, eliminating collisions between devices on different switch ports.

questions.question: What criteria is used by a Cisco LAN switch to decide how to forward Ethernet frames?
questions.explanation: Cisco LAN switches use the destination MAC address and the MAC address table to make Ethernet frame forwarding decisions.

questions.question: What are two reasons a network administrator would segment a network with a Layer 2 switch?
options: To isolate ARP request messages from the rest of the network
questions.explanation: Layer 2 switching creates microsegmented connections that can give devices full-bandwidth, full-duplex connectivity during transmission and can isolate traffic between segments. Layer 2 switches do not isolate broadcasts such as ARP requests.

questions.question: A switch has received a frame on an ingress port. What will the switch do if the unicast destination MAC address is in the MAC address table?
options: It will forward the frame out all ports.
It will forward the frame out all ports except the incoming port.
It will forward the frame out of the specified port in the MAC address table.
questions.explanation: If the destination MAC address is in the MAC address table, the switch forwards the frame out of the specified port.

questions.question: A switch has received a frame on an ingress port. What will the switch do if the unicast destination MAC address is not in the MAC address table?
options: It will forward the frame out all ports.
It will forward the frame out all ports except the incoming port.
It will forward the frame out of the specified port in the MAC address table.
questions.explanation: If the unicast destination MAC address is unknown, the switch floods the frame out all ports except the incoming port. This is called unknown unicast flooding.

questions.question: A switch has received a frame on an ingress port. What will the switch do if the destination MAC address is a broadcast address?
options: It will forward the frame out all ports.
It will forward the frame out all ports except the incoming port.
It will forward the frame out of the specified port in the MAC address table.
questions.explanation: If the destination MAC address is broadcast or multicast, the switch floods the frame out all ports except the incoming port.

questions.question: Which switching method forwards the frame immediately after examining the destination MAC address?
questions.explanation: Cut-through switching can make a forwarding decision as soon as it reads and looks up the destination MAC address in the MAC address table.

questions.question: Which statement about half-duplex and full-duplex communication is true?
options: Gigabit Ethernet and 10 Gb/s NICs can operate in full-duplex or half-duplex.
Half-duplex communication allows both ends to transmit and receive simultaneously.
Half-duplex communication is unidirectional, or one direction at a time.
questions.explanation: Full-duplex communication allows simultaneous sending and receiving. Half-duplex communication is one direction at a time. Gigabit Ethernet and 10 Gb/s NICs require full duplex and do not support half-duplex operation.

questions.question: Which port state will switch ports immediately transition to when configured for PortFast?
questions.explanation: PortFast allows a switch port to bypass the listening and learning states and transition immediately to the forwarding state.

questions.question: After the election of the root bridge has been completed, how will switches find the best paths to the root bridge?
options: Each switch will analyze the port states of all neighbors and use the designated ports to forward traffic to the root.
Each switch will analyze the sum of all port costs to reach the root and use the path with the lowest cost.
Each switch will analyze the sum of the hops to reach the root and use the path with the fewest hops.
Each switch will analyze the BID of all neighbors to reach the root and use the path through the lowest BID neighbors.
questions.explanation: After the root bridge is elected, each switch determines the best path to the root bridge by summing the individual port costs along each path. The path with the lowest total cost is selected.

questions.question: Which is the default STP operation mode on Cisco Catalyst switches?
questions.explanation: Cisco switches running IOS 15.0 or later run PVST+ by default. Cisco Catalyst switches support PVST+, Rapid PVST+, and MSTP, but only one mode can be active at a time.

questions.question: What value determines the root bridge when all switches connected by trunk links have default STP configurations?
questions.explanation: When all switches use the same default bridge priority, the MAC address becomes the deciding factor in the root bridge election. For a given VLAN, the extended system ID is also the same across the switches.

questions.question: During the implementation of Spanning Tree Protocol, all switches are rebooted by the network administrator. What is the first step of the spanning-tree election process?
options: All the switches send out BPDUs advertising themselves as the root bridge.
Each switch determines the best path to forward traffic.
Each switch determines what port to block to prevent a loop from occurring.
Each switch with a lower root ID than its neighbor will not send BPDUs.
questions.explanation: After a Cisco switch boots, it sends BPDUs containing its own BID and initially advertises itself as the root bridge. After the root bridge is elected, paths and port states are selected.

questions.question: Which two concepts relate to a switch port that is intended to have only end devices attached and intended never to be used to connect to another switch? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: The RSTP edge port concept corresponds to the Cisco PVST+ PortFast feature. An edge port connects to an end station and should immediately transition to forwarding.

questions.question: Which three port states are used by Rapid PVST+? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Rapid PVST+ uses the discarding, learning, and forwarding port states.

questions.question: When PVST is running over a switched network, which port state can participate in BPDU frame forwarding based on BPDUs received, but does not forward data frames?
questions.explanation: Ports in the listening state can participate in BPDU frame forwarding based on received BPDUs, but they do not forward data frames.

questions.question: Which STP port role is adopted by a switch port if there is no other port with a lower cost to the root bridge?
questions.explanation: The root port is the port on a non-root switch with the lowest path cost to reach the root bridge.

questions.question: Which two statements describe a switch port that is configured with PortFast? (Choose two.)
options: The switch port immediately transitions from the listening to the forwarding state.
The switch port immediately transitions from blocking to the forwarding state.
The switch port sends DHCP requests before transitioning to the forwarding state.
The switch port immediately processes any BPDUs before transitioning to the forwarding state.
The switch port should never receive BPDUs.
questions.explanation: A PortFast port immediately transitions from blocking to forwarding. PortFast should only be configured on ports connected to end devices, so the port should never receive BPDUs.

questions.question: What is one way to correct a spanning tree failure?
options: Replace the cables on failed STP links.
Manually remove redundant links in the switched network.
Insert redundant links to replace the failed STP links.
Replace all instances of STP with RSTP.
questions.explanation: When a spanning tree failure creates Layer 2 loops, removing redundant links in the failed segment can normalize traffic and CPU load while the STP issue is investigated.

questions.question: What additional information is contained in the 12-bit extended system ID of a BPDU?
questions.explanation: The extended system ID is a 12-bit field in the bridge ID that identifies the VLAN ID.

questions.question: An administrator is troubleshooting a switch and wants to verify if it is a root bridge. What command can be used to do this?
questions.explanation: The show spanning-tree command displays STP information, including root bridge details.

questions.question: What is an accurate description of redundancy?
options: designing a network to use multiple virtual devices to ensure that all traffic uses the best path through the internetwork
configuring a router with a complete MAC address database to ensure that all frames can be forwarded to the correct destination
designing a network to use multiple paths between switches to ensure there is no single point of failure
configuring a switch with proper security to ensure that all traffic forwarded through an interface is filtered
questions.explanation: Redundancy removes single points of failure by using multiple physical paths between switches in the network.

questions.question: Which three components are combined to form a bridge ID? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: The bridge ID consists of the bridge priority, extended system ID, and MAC address.

questions.question: What is an advantage of PVST+?
options: PVST+ optimizes performance on the network through automatic selection of the root bridge.
PVST+ optimizes performance on the network through load sharing using multiple root bridges.
PVST+ reduces bandwidth consumption compared to traditional implementations of STP that use CST.
PVST+ requires fewer CPU cycles for all the switches in the network.
questions.explanation: PVST+ can optimize load sharing by allowing different VLANs to use different root bridges. This requires manual configuration; root bridges are not automatically selected for load sharing.

questions.question: In which two port states does a switch learn MAC addresses and process BPDUs in a PVST network? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Switches learn MAC addresses in the learning and forwarding states. They process BPDUs in the blocking, listening, learning, and forwarding states.

questions.question: What two features does Spanning Tree Protocol (STP) provide to ensure proper network operations? (Choose two.)
options: Link-state dynamic routing that provides redundant routes
Removing single points of failure with multiple Layer 2 switches
questions.explanation: STP supports correct operation when a network has multiple interconnected Layer 2 switches and redundant links that remove single points of failure.

questions.question: Which PVST+ feature ensures that configured switch edge ports do not cause Layer 2 loops if a port is mistakenly connected to another switch?
questions.explanation: BPDU guard places an edge port into an error-disabled state if the port receives a BPDU. This helps prevent Layer 2 loops when a PortFast edge port is connected incorrectly.

questions.question: What is an advantage of using STP in a LAN?
options: It combines multiple switch trunk links into a logical port channel link to increase bandwidth.
It decreases the size of the failure domain.
It provides firewall services to protect the LAN.
It temporarily disables redundant paths to stop Layer 2 loops.
questions.explanation: STP allows redundant physical connections between Layer 2 devices without creating Layer 2 loops by temporarily disabling ports that could create a loop.

questions.question: Which two statements regarding a PortFast enabled switch port are true? (Choose two.)
options: The port immediately transitions from blocking to forwarding state.
The port immediately transitions from listening to forwarding state.
The port immediately processes any BPDUs before transitioning to the forwarding state.
The port sends DHCP requests before transitioning to the forwarding state.
The port should never receive BPDUs.
questions.explanation: PortFast-enabled ports immediately transition from blocking to forwarding and should only be used on access ports connected to end devices. Such ports should never receive BPDUs.
